acceptance: A committed test classifies all 99 queries into (a), (b) or (c) with a derived-value flag
The test passes with an xfail list that may only shrink
The category counts are recorded in this item, with the decision on the 15-query gate
context:
Source: DataFrame query parity proposal v3 (item T2). Do not prototype adapters on Q41; it is the negative control. Project owner does NOT accept earlier reviewers' TPC-H claims.

Progress 2026-10-01: implemented as PR #2520 (branch feat/tpcds-parameter-consumption-inventory, worktree ../BenchBox.wt-tpcds-param-inventory, head 82ead60d2 after merging develop); make pr-preflight exit 0 before the merge. tests/unit/core/tpcds/test_parameter_consumption_inventory.py: 41 passed, 64 strict xfails, about 13 s (medium lane; skipped without SIGALRM, i.e. Windows). METHOD (TESTED): patch queries.get_parameters with a recorder and run both families of all 99 queries against a permissive stand-in context (194 of 198 implementations run to completion; pandas Q5, Q77, Q80, Q88 do not, so their dead-key result is a lower bound, tracked per query and family); join with the defaults file, the dsqgen -LOG names (generate_parameter_log) and the template text (which names reach the SQL, transitively through defines). COUNTS after review: hard-coded (c) 8 = Q16, 24, 41, 73, 74, 85, 88, 89 (the implementation reads a scalar or no matching key, so the code must change); binding gap (b) 56, including the 15 literal fallbacks, which match the earlier mock scan exactly (8, 10, 21, 23, 33, 34, 41, 45, 49, 54, 83, 84, 88, 90, 91), dead YAML keys (54 queries among complete runs), and list-valued defaults shorter than the draw (Q8, Q27, Q36: the implementation passes the whole list through, so only the binding data is short, adapter work with no code change); no gap detected (a) 35; derived-value templates 44 (e.g. Q39 [MONTH]+1). The first version called Q8, Q27 and Q36 hard-coded (11 in all) because it compared a default list's length with the draw; an automated review correctly pointed out that measures the sample default, not what the code can take. GATE DECISION: (c) = 8, under the 15-query gate, so the adapter and rewrite work can stay one program; caveat: 34 queries have single-valued dsqgen names the name-matching heuristic cannot pair (listed in the inventory but not counted), so 8 is a lower-bound estimate and should be rechecked after the t04 prototype. LIMITS: name matching is heuristic, so (a) means no gap detected, not verified. The classification lists are strict xfails that may only shrink. Remaining: hosted CI, merge, then finish.
description: Classify each of the 99 queries by whether its DataFrame implementation consumes the parameters dsqgen produces: (a) keys match, (b) literal fallback or dead YAML keys, (c) hard-coded semantics (Q41 hard-codes four color pairs where the SQL has 16 colors x units x sizes; Q8 uses 5 of 400 zips). Also flag queries needing derived values (Q39 [MONTH]+1). A prior mock-based scan found 15 queries reading keys absent from default_parameters.yaml with silent literal fallback (8, 10, 21, 23, 33, 34, 41, 45, 49, 54, 83, 84, 88, 90, 91) and up to 58 with unread YAML keys; it stops at the first exception, so treat counts as lower bounds (unverified by me beyond Q41). The test runs without data (dsqgen only, about 4 s). Gate: if category (c) exceeds about 15 queries, the adapter and rewrite work must be budgeted as a separate program.
